ramayana-2-23-7.translation: Seeing his pale, sweating, troubled face, she, tormented by sorrow, said: What is this now, lord?
ramayana-2-23-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-8.translation: Today the glorious Pushya, ruled by Brihaspati, is in conjunction, the wise brahmins say. Why are you troubled, Raghava?
ramayana-2-23-8.meaning: It should be a happy day.
ramayana-2-23-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-9.translation: Your lovely face is not shaded by the hundred-ribbed umbrella, white as water-foam.
ramayana-2-23-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-10.translation: Your lotus-eyed face is not being fanned by the two fine whisks, bright as the moon and swans.
ramayana-2-23-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-11.translation: The eloquent bards and heralds are not seen joyfully praising you today with blessings, bull among men.
ramayana-2-23-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-12.translation: Brahmins learned in the Vedas are not pouring honey and curd on your head as prescribed for one being anointed.
ramayana-2-23-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-13.translation: The ministers, the heads of guilds in their finery, and the people of town and country do not want to follow you.
ramayana-2-23-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-14.translation: Why does the fine Pushya chariot, yoked to four swift horses adorned with gold, not go before you?
ramayana-2-23-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-15.translation: No splendid elephant with auspicious marks, like a dark cloud-mountain, is seen going before you, hero.
ramayana-2-23-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-16.translation: Nor do I see the gold-patterned throne carried before you as you go, handsome one, with heroes in front.
ramayana-2-23-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-17.translation: When the coronation was ready, what is this now? Your face has a colour I have never seen, and no joy shows.
ramayana-2-23-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-18.translation: To her lamenting like this, the joy of the Raghus said: Sita, my revered father is banishing me to the forest.
ramayana-2-23-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-19.translation: Born in a great family, knowing and practising dharma, hear, Janaki, how this has come to me step by step.
ramayana-2-23-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-20.translation: My father, King Dasharatha, true to his word, long ago gladly gave Kaikeyi two great boons.
ramayana-2-23-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-21.translation: Today, when the coronation was ready and the king had prepared it, she claimed that agreement, and he was overcome by dharma.
ramayana-2-23-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-22.translation: I must live fourteen years in Dandaka, and father has appointed Bharata crown prince. So I have come to see you as I leave for the lonely forest.
ramayana-2-23-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-23.translation: Never praise me near Bharata; prosperous men cannot bear praise of others. So do not speak of my virtues before Bharata.
ramayana-2-23-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-24.translation: Do not expect special treatment from him; you can live near him by being agreeable.
ramayana-2-23-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-25.translation: Keeping my father's promise, I will go to the forest today. Be steadfast, wise one.
ramayana-2-23-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-26.translation: When I have gone to the forest where sages live, blessed and sinless one, you should devote yourself to vows and fasts.
ramayana-2-23-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-27.translation: Rising early and worshipping the gods properly, you should honour my father, King Dasharatha.
ramayana-2-23-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-28.translation: My mother Kausalya, old and worn with sorrow, deserves respect from you, with dharma first.
ramayana-2-23-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-29.translation: You should always honour my other mothers too; in love, affection and care they are all equal to me as mothers.
ramayana-2-23-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama goes to Sita, who sees something is wrong. He tells her of the exile and asks her to stay in Ayodhya, honour his parents and live quietly under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-30.translation: You should look on Lakshmana and Shatrughna especially as brothers and sons; they are dearer to me than life.
ramayana-2-23-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama asks Sita to stay in Ayodhya and live tactfully under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-31.translation: Never do anything to displease Bharata; he is now king and lord of the land and the family.
ramayana-2-23-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama asks Sita to stay in Ayodhya and live tactfully under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-32.translation: Kings are pleased when served with good conduct and effort, and angered by the opposite.
ramayana-2-23-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama asks Sita to stay in Ayodhya and live tactfully under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-33.translation: Kings cast off even their own sons who act against them, and embrace capable people even if strangers.
ramayana-2-23-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama asks Sita to stay in Ayodhya and live tactfully under Bharata.

ramayana-2-23-34.translation: I will go to the great forest, beloved; you must live right here, lovely one. Do as I say, and give no one cause for offence.
ramayana-2-23-34.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 23: Rama asks Sita to stay in Ayodhya and live tactfully under Bharata.

ramayana-2-24-1.translation: Thus addressed, Vaidehi, who deserved kindness and spoke kindly, grew angry out of love and said to her husband:
ramayana-2-24-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-2.translation: Noble son, father, mother, brother, son and daughter-in-law each enjoy their own merit and meet their own fortune.
ramayana-2-24-2.meaning: Each person has their own lot.
ramayana-2-24-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-3.translation: But a wife alone shares her husband's fortune, bull among men. So I too am ordered to live in the forest.
ramayana-2-24-3.meaning: A wife shares her husband's lot, so she is exiled too.
ramayana-2-24-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-4.translation: Not father, nor son, nor self, nor mother, nor friends; for women, here and hereafter, the husband alone is always the refuge.
ramayana-2-24-4.meaning: Her husband is her refuge, as the text sees it.
ramayana-2-24-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-5.translation: If you are setting out today for the hard forest, Raghava, I will walk ahead of you, crushing the kusha grass and thorns.
ramayana-2-24-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-6.translation: Casting off jealousy and anger like leftover water, take me with you confidently, hero; there is no sin in me.
ramayana-2-24-6.meaning: She asks him to trust her.
ramayana-2-24-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-7.translation: Better than palace tops, flying chariots or travelling through the sky, in every condition, is the shade of a husband's feet.
ramayana-2-24-7.meaning: Being with him is better than any luxury.
ramayana-2-24-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-8.translation: My mother and father have taught me in many ways; I need not be told now how to behave.
ramayana-2-24-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-9.translation: I will live happily in the forest just as in my father's house, thinking not of the three worlds but of my vow to my husband.
ramayana-2-24-9.meaning: She will be content with him.
ramayana-2-24-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-10.translation: Always serving you, disciplined and chaste, I will delight with you, hero, in the honey-scented forests.
ramayana-2-24-10.meaning: She looks forward to their life together.
ramayana-2-24-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-11.translation: You can protect others in the forest, Rama; how much more me, giver of honour.
ramayana-2-24-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-12.translation: I will live on fruits and roots, no doubt; I will cause you no trouble living with you.
ramayana-2-24-12.meaning: She will not be a burden.
ramayana-2-24-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-13.translation: I want to see rivers, mountains, ponds and forests everywhere without fear, with you, my wise protector.
ramayana-2-24-13.meaning: She is eager to see nature.
ramayana-2-24-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-14.translation: I would happily see lotus ponds in full bloom, crowded with swans and ducks, together with you, my hero.
ramayana-2-24-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-15.translation: With you I will delight in great joy, wide-eyed one, even for a hundred thousand years with you.
ramayana-2-24-15.meaning: She wants a lifetime with him.
ramayana-2-24-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-16.translation: Even living in heaven, if it were without you, Raghava, tiger among men, I would not want it.
ramayana-2-24-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-17.translation: I will go to the impassable forest full of deer, monkeys and elephants; I will live there as in my father's house, holding your feet, honoured.
ramayana-2-24-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-18.translation: Devoted to no one else, my heart attached to you, resolved to die if parted from you, take me, grant my request; I will not be a burden to you.
ramayana-2-24-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-24-19.translation: Though she spoke so, the best of men, devoted to dharma, did not wish to take Sita, and spoke at length to turn her back, grieved at the thought of her living in the forest.
ramayana-2-24-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 24: Sita refuses to stay behind. A wife shares her husband's fortune, she says; she will walk ahead of him, crushing thorns, and the forest with him will be happier than a palace.

ramayana-2-25-1.translation: To Sita speaking like this, righteous Rama, knowing dharma, said this to turn her back:
ramayana-2-25-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-2.translation: Sita, you come of a great family and are always devoted to dharma. Practise your own dharma here; do not follow your heart's pleasure.
ramayana-2-25-2.meaning: Stay and do your duty here.
ramayana-2-25-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-3.translation: Sita, do as I tell you, my gentle one; the forest has many dangers. Hear them as I tell them.
ramayana-2-25-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-4.translation: Sita, give up this idea of living in the forest. The wilderness is said to be full of dangers.
ramayana-2-25-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-5.translation: I say this for your good. I know no happiness in the forest; the forest is always sorrow.
ramayana-2-25-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-6.translation: The roars of lions living in mountain caves, echoing from mountain waterfalls, are painful to hear; so the forest is sorrow.
ramayana-2-25-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-7.translation: One sleeps at night on beds of leaves broken by oneself on the ground, worn out with toil; so the forest is more sorrowful.
ramayana-2-25-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-8.translation: One must fast as much as life allows, Maithili, wear a mass of matted hair and dress in bark.
ramayana-2-25-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-9.translation: Fierce wind, darkness and constant hunger, and great dangers: so the forest is more sorrowful.
ramayana-2-25-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-10.translation: Many reptiles of many forms roam the earth boldly, lovely one; so the forest is more sorrowful.
ramayana-2-25-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-11.translation: Snakes living in rivers, moving crookedly like rivers, lie across the path; so the forest is more sorrowful.
ramayana-2-25-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-12.translation: Moths, scorpions, insects, gadflies and mosquitoes always torment one, gentle woman; so the forest is all sorrow.
ramayana-2-25-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-13.translation: Thorny trees, kusha and kasha grasses, and tangled branches fill the forest, lovely one; so the forest is more sorrowful.
ramayana-2-25-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-14.translation: So enough of going to the forest; the forest is not right for you. Thinking it over, I see the forest has many more dangers.
ramayana-2-25-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-25-15.translation: Great Rama had not resolved to take her to the forest; Sita did not accept his words, and in great sorrow said this to Rama:
ramayana-2-25-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 25: Rama describes the hardships of forest life (wild beasts, snakes, hunger, thorns) to persuade Sita to stay.

ramayana-2-26-1.translation: Hearing Rama's words, Sita, grieved, her face streaming with tears, spoke softly:
ramayana-2-26-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-2.translation: The dangers you named of living in the forest, know them to be blessings, when love comes first.
ramayana-2-26-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-3.translation: I must go with you, by the command of my elders; separated from you, Rama, I must give up my life here.
ramayana-2-26-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-4.translation: With me near you, Raghava, not even Indra, lord of the gods, could overpower me by force.
ramayana-2-26-4.meaning: She is safest at his side.
ramayana-2-26-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-5.translation: A woman without her husband cannot live; you yourself have shown me this, Rama.
ramayana-2-26-5.meaning: She cannot live apart from him.
ramayana-2-26-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-6.translation: And, wise one, I heard from brahmins long ago in my father's house that I would truly have to live in a forest.
ramayana-2-26-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-7.translation: Hearing those words at home from brahmins who read signs, I have always been eager to live in the forest, mighty one.
ramayana-2-26-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-8.translation: That command to live in the forest must come to me; so I will go there with you, dear, and not otherwise.
ramayana-2-26-8.meaning: She will go only with him.
ramayana-2-26-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-9.translation: I will have fulfilled the prophecy; I will go with you. The time has come; let the brahmin's word be true.
ramayana-2-26-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-10.translation: I know there are many sorrows in forest life, but they surely fall on men whose minds are not disciplined, hero.
ramayana-2-26-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-11.translation: As a girl in my father's house I heard of forest life from a good-living woman mendicant, before my mother.
ramayana-2-26-11.meaning: She has heard of forest life.
ramayana-2-26-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-12.translation: And earlier I begged you many times, lord, wishing to go to live in the forest with you.
ramayana-2-26-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-13.translation: I have been waiting for this chance, Raghava, bless you. The life of a hero's forest dwelling pleases me.
ramayana-2-26-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-14.translation: Pure-souled one, through love I will be free of sin, following my husband, for my husband is my god.
ramayana-2-26-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-15.translation: Even after death my union with you will be blessed; this holy teaching is heard from famous brahmins.
ramayana-2-26-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-16.translation: A woman given to a man in this world by her parents with water, by their own dharma, is his even after death.
ramayana-2-26-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-17.translation: So why do you not wish to take me, your own wife, of good conduct and devoted to her husband?
ramayana-2-26-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-18.translation: Devoted, faithful, wretched, the same in joy and sorrow, you should take me, Kakutstha, sharing your joys and sorrows.
ramayana-2-26-18.meaning: Take me as your equal partner.
ramayana-2-26-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-19.translation: If you do not wish to take me, grieving like this, to the forest, I will take poison, fire or water to die.
ramayana-2-26-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-20.translation: So she begged him in many ways to go, but the mighty-armed one did not agree to take her to the lonely forest.
ramayana-2-26-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-21.translation: Thus answered, Maithili fell into deep thought, as if bathing the ground with the hot tears falling from her eyes.
ramayana-2-26-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-26-22.translation: Self-possessed Kakutstha comforted Vaidehi much, seeing her thoughtful and angry, to turn her back.
ramayana-2-26-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 26: Sita answers that with Rama the hardships are blessings, that brahmins once foretold she would live in a forest, and that she will die rather than be left behind.

ramayana-2-27-1.translation: Being comforted by Rama, Maithili, Janaka's daughter, said this to her husband about going to the forest:
ramayana-2-27-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-2.translation: Deeply agitated, out of love and pride, Sita rebuked broad-chested Raghava.
ramayana-2-27-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-3.translation: What did my father, the Videha lord of Mithila, think, Rama, gaining you as son-in-law, a woman in a man's form?
ramayana-2-27-3.meaning: A sharp challenge to his courage.
ramayana-2-27-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-4.translation: It would be a lie, which ignorant people would tell, that there is no greater power than Rama's, blazing like the sun.
ramayana-2-27-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-5.translation: What have you done that you are so downcast, and what do you fear, that you want to abandon me, who has no other refuge?
ramayana-2-27-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-6.translation: Know me to be like Savitri, devoted to Satyavan son of Dyumatsena, one who follows you alone.
ramayana-2-27-6.meaning: She compares herself to Savitri, who followed her husband even to Death.
ramayana-2-27-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-7.translation: I would not even in my mind look at another man but you, sinless one. I would go with you, Raghava, not like some woman who disgraces her family.
ramayana-2-27-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-8.translation: You yourself want to hand me over to others like an actor, your wife married young and long living with you, chaste.
ramayana-2-27-8.meaning: She is hurt by being left.
ramayana-2-27-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-9.translation: You should not set out for the forest without taking me. Austerity, forest or heaven, let it be with you.
ramayana-2-27-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-10.translation: I will feel no weariness on the road, walking behind you, nor in resting or sleeping.
ramayana-2-27-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-11.translation: Kusha and kasha grass, reeds and thorny trees will feel to me like cotton and deerskin on the road with you.
ramayana-2-27-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-12.translation: The dust stirred by great winds that covers me, beloved, I will think of as precious sandalwood.
ramayana-2-27-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-13.translation: When I sit on grassy meadows at the forest's edge, roaming the forest, what could be happier than beds with fine covers?
ramayana-2-27-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-14.translation: Leaf, root or fruit, little or much, that you yourself bring and give me, will taste like nectar.
ramayana-2-27-14.meaning: Simple food from him is sweet.
ramayana-2-27-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-15.translation: There I will not remember mother, father or home, enjoying the flowers and fruits of each season.
ramayana-2-27-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-16.translation: You will see nothing unpleasant there; you will not grieve because of me, and I will not be hard to look after.
ramayana-2-27-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-17.translation: Where you are is heaven; where you are not is hell. Knowing this, Rama, go with me in the highest joy.
ramayana-2-27-17.meaning: Her famous words: with him is heaven.
ramayana-2-27-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-18.translation: If you will not take me, untroubled as I am, to the forest, I will drink poison today rather than fall into enemies' power.
ramayana-2-27-18.meaning: She will not be left behind.
ramayana-2-27-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-19.translation: Afterwards, through grief, I would not live anyway; abandoned by you, lord, death then would be better.
ramayana-2-27-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-20.translation: I cannot bear this grief for even a moment; how much less for ten, three and one years in sorrow.
ramayana-2-27-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-21.translation: So, burning with grief, after lamenting pitifully, she cried out loud, clinging tightly to her husband.
ramayana-2-27-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-22.translation: Wounded by many words as an elephant cow by poisoned arrows, she released her long-held tears as a fire-stick releases fire.
ramayana-2-27-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-23.translation: Crystal-clear water born of distress flowed from her eyes like water from lotuses.
ramayana-2-27-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-24.translation: Embracing her with his arms as she seemed to faint with grief, Rama, reassuring her, said:
ramayana-2-27-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-25.translation: Queen, I would not want even heaven at the cost of your grief. I have no fear of anything, like Brahma himself.
ramayana-2-27-25.meaning: He would not hurt her for anything.
ramayana-2-27-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-26.translation: Not knowing your full intent, lovely one, I did not want you to live in the forest, though I am able to protect you.
ramayana-2-27-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-27.translation: Since you were made to live in the forest with me, Maithili, I cannot leave you, as a self-possessed man cannot abandon his good name.
ramayana-2-27-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-28.translation: Dharma was practised by the good of old, elephant-thighed one, and I follow it today as Suvarchala follows the sun.
ramayana-2-27-28.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-29.translation: This dharma, lovely one, is obedience to father and mother; so I cannot live if I break their command.
ramayana-2-27-29.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Sita, hurt and proud, challenges Rama: did her father marry her to a woman in a man's form? Where he is, is heaven. Moved by her tears, Rama agrees she will come. A celebrated portrait of Sita's courage and devotion.

ramayana-2-27-30.translation: As my father, standing on the path of truth and dharma, commands me, so I wish to act; that is eternal dharma. Follow me, timid one, and be my partner in dharma.
ramayana-2-27-30.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Rama agrees that Sita will come and asks her to give away their wealth.

ramayana-2-27-31.translation: Give jewels to brahmins and food to mendicants and to those who ask; hurry, without delay.
ramayana-2-27-31.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Rama agrees that Sita will come and asks her to give away their wealth.

ramayana-2-27-32.translation: Knowing her husband agreed to her going, the queen, delighted, quickly began to give.
ramayana-2-27-32.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Rama agrees that Sita will come and asks her to give away their wealth.

ramayana-2-27-33.translation: Then, delighted and fulfilled, the famous, high-minded lady, seeing her husband's words, began to give away wealth and jewels to the righteous.
ramayana-2-27-33.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 27: Rama agrees that Sita will come and asks her to give away their wealth.

ramayana-2-28-1.translation: Then mighty Rama spoke to Lakshmana, who stood before him with folded hands, ready to go first, begging:
ramayana-2-28-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-2.translation: If you go to the forest with me today, Saumitri, who will look after Kausalya or famous Sumitra?
ramayana-2-28-2.meaning: Who will care for the mothers?
ramayana-2-28-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-3.translation: The mighty king, who showered the earth with gifts like a rain cloud, is caught in the noose of desire.
ramayana-2-28-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-4.translation: When the daughter of King Ashvapati gains this kingdom, she will not treat her grieving co-wives well.
ramayana-2-28-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-5.translation: Thus addressed gently by Rama, Lakshmana, skilled in speech, replied to eloquent Rama:
ramayana-2-28-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-6.translation: By your power alone, hero, Bharata will carefully honour Kausalya and Sumitra; there is no doubt.
ramayana-2-28-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-7.translation: Noble Kausalya could support a thousand like me; she has a thousand villages for her living.
ramayana-2-28-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-8.translation: Taking my bow and arrows, carrying spade and basket, I will go ahead of you showing the way.
ramayana-2-28-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-9.translation: I will always bring you roots and fruits and whatever other forest food is fit for ascetics.
ramayana-2-28-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-10.translation: You will enjoy yourself with Vaidehi on the mountain slopes; I will do everything, while you wake and while you sleep.
ramayana-2-28-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-11.translation: Well pleased by these words, Rama replied: Go, Saumitri, take leave of all your friends.
ramayana-2-28-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-12.translation: The two divine, fearsome bows that great Varuna himself gave the king at Janaka's great sacrifice,
ramayana-2-28-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-13.translation: the divine impenetrable armour, the two quivers of inexhaustible arrows, and the two gold-adorned swords bright as the sun,
ramayana-2-28-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-14.translation: all kept with honour in our teacher's house: take these weapons and come back quickly, Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-28-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-15.translation: Resolved on forest life, he took leave of his friends, took leave of the Ikshvaku teacher and took the fine weapons.
ramayana-2-28-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-16.translation: Saumitri showed Rama all the divine weapons, honoured and adorned with garlands.
ramayana-2-28-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-17.translation: Self-possessed Rama lovingly said to Lakshmana: You have come at the time I wished, gentle Lakshmana.
ramayana-2-28-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-18.translation: I want to give away this wealth of mine to brahmins and ascetics with you, tamer of foes.
ramayana-2-28-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-19.translation: The best of brahmins who live here with firm devotion to our elders, and all my dependants too,
ramayana-2-28-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-28-20.translation: bring quickly noble Suyajna, son of Vasishtha, best of brahmins. I will go to the forest after honouring him and all the other learned brahmins.
ramayana-2-28-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 28: Lakshmana insists on coming too, promising to serve Rama and Sita in the forest. Rama asks him to fetch the divine weapons kept with their teacher.

ramayana-2-29-1.translation: Understanding his brother's kind and welcome command, he went and quickly entered Suyajna's house.
ramayana-2-29-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-2.translation: Bowing to the brahmin in his fire-room, Lakshmana said: Friend, come and see the house of one doing a hard thing.
ramayana-2-29-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-3.translation: After the evening prayer he quickly went with Saumitri and entered Rama's lovely, splendid house.
ramayana-2-29-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-4.translation: Raghava with Sita came forward with folded hands to the learned Suyajna, as to a worshipped fire.
ramayana-2-29-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-5.translation: With fine gold armlets, lovely earrings, gold threads with gems, bracelets and bangles,
ramayana-2-29-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-6.translation: and many other jewels Kakutstha honoured him, and Rama, urged by Sita, said to Suyajna:
ramayana-2-29-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-7.translation: Take this necklace and gold chain for your wife, gentle one; and Sita wants to give you her girdle now, friend.
ramayana-2-29-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-8.translation: Vaidehi also wants to give you this couch with a fine cover, adorned with many jewels.
ramayana-2-29-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-9.translation: The elephant named Shatrunjaya that my uncle gave me, I give you with a thousand elephants, best of brahmins.
ramayana-2-29-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-10.translation: Thus addressed by Rama, Suyajna accepted it and gave auspicious blessings to Rama, Lakshmana and Sita.
ramayana-2-29-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-11.translation: Then kind-spoken Rama said to his calm, dear brother Saumitri, as Brahma speaks to Indra:
ramayana-2-29-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-12.translation: Invite and honour with jewels the two best of brahmins, Agastya and Kaushika, as crops are refreshed with rain.
ramayana-2-29-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-13.translation: The devoted teacher of the Taittiriya school, handsome and learned, who serves Kausalya with blessings,
ramayana-2-29-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-14.translation: give him a carriage, servant women and silk clothes until that brahmin is satisfied, Saumitri.
ramayana-2-29-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-15.translation: And noble Chitraratha, the charioteer and long-serving counsellor, please him with costly jewels, clothes and wealth.
ramayana-2-29-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-16.translation: And a thousand loads of rice, two hundred oxen and, for dairy, a thousand cows, Saumitri.
ramayana-2-29-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-17.translation: Then Lakshmana, tiger among men, himself gave that wealth to the best brahmins as instructed, like Kubera.
ramayana-2-29-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-18.translation: Then he spoke to the dependants standing there, choked with tears, having given much to each one:
ramayana-2-29-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-19.translation: Keep Lakshmana's house and this home of mine each occupied until I return.
ramayana-2-29-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-20.translation: Having said this to all those grieving dependants, he told the treasurer: Bring the wealth. And the dependants brought all his wealth.
ramayana-2-29-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-21.translation: Then the tiger among men with Lakshmana had it given to brahmins, children, the old and the poor.
ramayana-2-29-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-22.translation: There was a brahmin there named Trijata of the Garga clan, tawny-haired; no one stopped him up to the fifth courtyard.
ramayana-2-29-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-23.translation: Reaching the prince, Trijata said: I am poor with many sons, famous prince. I live by gleaning in the forest; look after me.
ramayana-2-29-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-24.translation: Rama, in a playful mood, said to him: I have not yet given away even one thousand cows. As far as you can throw your staff, you will get that many.
ramayana-2-29-24.meaning: A gentle joke and a generous offer.
ramayana-2-29-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-25.translation: He quickly, eagerly tied his cloth round his waist, whirled his staff and threw it with all his strength.
ramayana-2-29-25.meaning: Trijata throws with all his might.
ramayana-2-29-25.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-26.translation: Then Rama, comforting that Garga, said: Do not be offended; this was just my joke.
ramayana-2-29-26.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-29-27.translation: Then the great sage Trijata with his wife, receiving a herd of cows, delighted, gave great Rama blessings that increase fame, strength, love and happiness.
ramayana-2-29-27.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 29: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana give away their wealth to brahmins, teachers, servants and the poor, including a playful gift to the poor brahmin Trijata.

ramayana-2-30-1.translation: Having given much wealth to brahmins with Vaidehi, the two Raghavas went with Sita to see their father.
ramayana-2-30-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-2.translation: The weapons they carried, hard to look at, shone, hung with garlands and adorned by Sita.
ramayana-2-30-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-3.translation: Then the people climbed palaces, mansions and towers and watched sorrowfully.
ramayana-2-30-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-4.translation: The streets were too crowded to walk, so they climbed the palaces and gazed sadly at Raghava.
ramayana-2-30-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-5.translation: Seeing Rama on foot, without his umbrella, the people, stricken with grief, said many things.
ramayana-2-30-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-6.translation: He whom a great four-part army used to follow is followed now only by Lakshmana with Sita.
ramayana-2-30-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-7.translation: Though he knows the taste of power and grants desires, he will not make his father a liar, out of reverence for dharma.
ramayana-2-30-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-8.translation: Sita, whom even beings in the sky could not see before, the people on the royal road see today.
ramayana-2-30-8.meaning: Sita is seen in public for the first time.
ramayana-2-30-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-9.translation: Sita, used to cosmetics and red sandal paste, will soon be darkened by rain, heat and cold.
ramayana-2-30-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-10.translation: Surely Dasharatha speaks today possessed by some spirit; no king would banish his dear son.
ramayana-2-30-10.meaning: They think the king is not himself.
ramayana-2-30-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-11.translation: How could even a worthless son be banished? How much more one who has won this world by his conduct alone?
ramayana-2-30-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-12.translation: Kindness, compassion, learning, character, self-control and calm: these six virtues adorn Raghava, best of men.
ramayana-2-30-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-13.translation: So the people are deeply pained by his injury, like water creatures when the water dries up in summer.
ramayana-2-30-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-14.translation: The whole world is pained by the pain of this lord of the world, as a flowering, fruiting tree is when its root is cut.
ramayana-2-30-14.meaning: Rama is the root of their happiness.
ramayana-2-30-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-15.translation: Like Lakshmana, let us quickly follow where Raghava goes, with our wives and kin.
ramayana-2-30-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-16.translation: Leaving gardens, fields and homes, sharing one sorrow and joy, let us follow righteous Rama.
ramayana-2-30-16.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-17.translation: Let Kaikeyi take our abandoned houses, their treasure dug up, courtyards ruined, grain and wealth removed, stripped of all value,
ramayana-2-30-17.meaning: They will leave the city empty.
ramayana-2-30-17.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-18.translation: covered in dust, deserted by the household gods, abandoned by us.
ramayana-2-30-18.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-19.translation: Let the forest where Raghava goes become a city, and let the city we abandon become a forest.
ramayana-2-30-19.meaning: The people go where Rama goes.
ramayana-2-30-19.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-20.translation: Let fanged beasts leave their dens, and deer and birds their slopes, and come to live in what we abandon.
ramayana-2-30-20.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-21.translation: Rama heard these many things said by all kinds of people, and hearing them, his mind did not change.
ramayana-2-30-21.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-22.translation: Looking at the distressed people, himself showing no distress, almost smiling, Rama went to see his father, wishing to do his command properly.
ramayana-2-30-22.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-23.translation: Before going, great Rama, Ikshvaku's son, about to leave for the forest, stood seeing Sumantra stricken, waiting to be announced to his father.
ramayana-2-30-23.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-30-24.translation: Devoted to dharma, resolved to enter the forest by his father's command, Raghava, seeing Sumantra, said: Announce my coming to the king.
ramayana-2-30-24.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 30: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana walk on foot to the king's palace as grieving crowds lament and vow to follow them, leaving Ayodhya empty for Kaikeyi.

ramayana-2-31-1.translation: Sent by Rama, the charioteer, his senses clouded by grief, went in quickly and saw the king sighing.
ramayana-2-31-1.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-2.translation: Seeing the king deeply troubled, grieving for Rama, the wise charioteer approached him with folded hands.
ramayana-2-31-2.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-3.translation: Here is your son at the door, tiger among men, having given all his wealth to brahmins and dependants.
ramayana-2-31-3.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-4.translation: Let Rama, true in valour, see you, bless you. Having taken leave of all his friends, he wishes to see you now.
ramayana-2-31-4.meaning: He has said goodbye to everyone.
ramayana-2-31-4.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-5.translation: He will go to the great forest; see him, lord of the earth, endowed with every kingly virtue like the sun with its rays.
ramayana-2-31-5.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-6.translation: The truthful, righteous king, deep as the ocean and clear as the sky, replied:
ramayana-2-31-6.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-7.translation: Sumantra, bring all my wives who are here; I want to see Raghava surrounded by all my wives.
ramayana-2-31-7.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-8.translation: Going into the inner palace he said to the women: The noble king calls you; go there without delay.
ramayana-2-31-8.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-9.translation: Thus told by Sumantra at the king's command, all the women went to that hall, knowing their husband's order.
ramayana-2-31-9.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-10.translation: Three hundred and fifty women with red-rimmed eyes, keeping their vows, slowly came surrounding Kausalya.
ramayana-2-31-10.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-11.translation: When the wives had come, the lord of the earth, seeing them, said to the charioteer: Sumantra, bring my son.
ramayana-2-31-11.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-12.translation: The charioteer, bringing Rama, Lakshmana and Maithili, went quickly towards the lord of the earth.
ramayana-2-31-12.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-13.translation: The king, seeing his son coming from afar with folded hands, sprang up from his seat, distressed, surrounded by the women.
ramayana-2-31-13.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-14.translation: The lord of people ran fast towards Rama, but before reaching him, stricken with grief, fell fainting to the ground.
ramayana-2-31-14.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.

ramayana-2-31-15.translation: Rama and the great warrior Lakshmana quickly rushed to the king, unconscious with grief and sorrow.
ramayana-2-31-15.explanation: Ayodhya Kanda, chapter 31: Dasharatha calls all his queens to see Rama, rushes towards his son and collapses.
